new_candidates.body:
### The feature, motivation and pitch

USD has the benefit of custom APIs, whereas mjSpec/mjcf needs text blobs or sidecar files to approximate the same function.

As an example for discussion, consider a python interface similar to h5py's `attrs`. Supporting any number of named "custom specs", which are flat dicts of key/value pairs, add-able to other mjSpec elements (bodies, sites, joints, actuators, etc):

```python
site # site(name="fid-site")

c = site.add_custom("fiducial")
c["label"] = "fid3"
c["id"] = 3
c["size"] = 0.01

c = site.get_custom("lidar")
c["model"] # "VLP-16"
c["range-m"] # numpy.array([0.5, 30])
```

Which serializes as

```xml
<site name="fid-site" pos...>
    <custom>
        <fiducial label="fid3" id="3" size="0.01"/>
        <lidar model="VLP-16" rotation-hz="10" elevations-deg="-10 -5 0 5 10" range-m="0.5 30"/>
    </custom>
</site>
```

To avoid silently-misspelled custom elements, let the spec also hold a section declaring the available custom specs. Perhaps this section could also be used to declare the attribute types to be used for those specs, so they are not lost in serialization nor inferred in deserialization.

### Alternatives

Using a `custom/text` block to hold a json blob with arbitrary data. This data does not follow `attach` calls, nor can it be used as part of a `default` class.

_No response_
